conviction_note: Two small positives offset two small negatives. The positives are a company with a record of raising its forecast and announcing returns at the print, holding ¥140.6bn of cash, with its ¥30bn buyback finished in May. The negatives are a soft Q3 already visible in the Q2 standalone 増収減益 and in the JEITA PC series, and a stock at an all-time high, sitting at the consensus target after a 13.4% run-in. The street's FY OP of ¥64.7bn already expects a raise, so the print is mostly about whether a buyback comes with it: p_up 52 on abs 3.0.
bar: Consensus FY2026 OP ¥64,686m and 経常 ¥66,026m (6 analysts, kabuyoho, as of 2026-10-23: https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=8060), against the company plan of OP ¥63,000m / 経常 ¥64,000m (raised from ¥60,000m on 2026-07-24: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260724/140120260721596814.pdf). The bar is the consensus number, one aggregator source. I expect the revised guide to land at about 64-65bn OP, i.e. at the bar.

findings.finding: The company plan implies H2 OP of ¥30.5bn, -1% YoY, after H1 OP of +18.9%. Q3 progress against plan should run about 69-71% against this company's own 66-68% at Q3 (2025: 38,201/58,188; 2024: 36,290/53,123). It raised at Q3 2025 (OP +¥1bn) and at Q2 2026 (+¥3bn), so a raise at this print is likely. But consensus FY OP of ¥64.7bn already sits 2.7% above plan, so a raise to about ¥65bn only meets the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raise at Q3 2025 (with returns): +7.92% (10-24 close to 10-27 close). Raise at Q2 2026 (OP +¥3bn, dividend raised): -0.48%. Q1 2026, OP +40.7% with no raise: +3.94%. Computed from Yahoo daily bars on the TDnet release dates.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The consensus of ¥64.7bn already discounts a raise of about ¥1.7bn. Only a raise beyond about ¥65bn, which needs Q3 OP above about ¥12bn against ¥10.9bn last year, would be new. If the market expected that, the consensus would sit above ¥65bn.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 短信 for the progress-rate history: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251024/140120251023577692.pdf. Consensus from kabuyoho: https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=8060

findings.finding: Capital returns have come with each recent print: Q3 2025 brought a ¥10bn buyback (1.84%) and a dividend raise to ¥160; FY2025 a ¥30bn buyback (4.66%) and a 2:1 split; Q2 2026 a dividend raise to ¥95 and a 100k-share ToSTNeT-3. The ¥30bn programme ended early, on 2026-05-21, and H1 cash stands at ¥140.6bn. The mid-term plan names 自己株式取得資金 and says buybacks will be done 機動的. A new buyback, and ¥5 more of dividend at a 40%+ payout on a raised NI, are both plausible here.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ¥10bn buyback with a dividend raise at Q3 2025: +7.92%. ¥30bn buyback with a split and the mid-term plan at FY2025: +0.74%. Dividend raise with a tiny ToSTNeT-3 at Q2 2026: -0.48%. Q2 2025 dividend raise with ToSTNeT-3: +4.28%. Mixed results, best when the buyback was new and sized.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a 13.4% run-in at an all-time high suggests some holders are positioned for returns. But a buyback is a board decision the market cannot see before 15:30, and nothing is outstanding after the May completion. If a buyback were fully expected, a no-buyback outcome would already be a known risk, and the -0.48% on Q2's tiny buyback says that risk exists.

findings.finding: Q3 momentum is soft. Q2 2026 standalone was 増収減益 (OP about ¥13.96bn against ¥14.16bn), as the company's own deck says, on the Windows 10 replacement 反動減. JEITA shows domestic PC shipment value at 82.2% (July) and 93.1% (August) of the prior year, against a Q3 2025 when ITプロダクト drove a record Q3 OP of ¥10.9bn.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. JEITA is public, and the company's H2 plan of -1% YoY OP already embeds the comp. What is left is whether the mix gains (SI +10%, services +8%) offset the PC drop by enough to beat the plan.

findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It says how much of a beat-and-raise the 13.4% run-in may already hold, and it largely agrees with the baseline lean of -0.81.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly positive (+0.5) against a baseline lean of -0.81 driven by the run-up. The strongest positive the release could carry is a fresh buyback with a dividend raise, and I looked: last year's Q3 did exactly that and the stock rose 7.92%. The positioning finding agrees with the run-up lean, so its size is kept small.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the soft-Q3 finding rests on the public JEITA series and a Q2 standalone anyone can compute from the last 短信, so it moved from -0.4 to -0.2.
Open question 4 (a run-in as a short signal, one case that went wrong): the positioning finding moved from -0.4 to -0.3.
Rule 2 (check the sign): I looked for the strongest positive (buyback, dividend). The two positives stand unchanged, and p_up moved from 50 to 52 because the negatives were trimmed.
